title: "Building Flow"
description: "Build the Flow binary from source: one static binary with the editor inside it, no C library underneath."
editUrl: false
---

HotLoop Flow is one static binary with the editor inside it, so most people pull the published image and never build anything. If you want your own build, the source is public, and a build needs Go and Node.

```bash
cd web && npm install && npm run build && cd ..
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -ldflags="-s -w" -o hotloop-flow ./cmd/hotloop-flow
```

The result is static, with no C library underneath, so it runs on a distroless image with nothing else installed. Every Flow release is built from a version tag and from nothing else, so the image on your plant floor is always one you can name and trace back to a release.
